# Upacālātherīgāthā (Thig 7.3)
**ID:** Thig 7.3

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Upacālātherīgāthā* (Thig 7.3) is a short poetic text in the seventh chapter (*Sattakanipāta*) of the *Therīgāthā*, belonging to the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. According to Pali tradition and secondary accounts, Upacālā was one of the three sisters of the Elder Sāriputta—along with Cālā and Sīsupacālā—who renounced household life to become Buddhist nuns and attained arahantship [Burlingame 1921; Nyanaponika et al. 2003; Horner 1940]. In the narrative associated with her verses, Māra approaches Upacālā while she is meditating in the forest and tempts her to aspire to rebirth among the celestial realms (such as the Tāvatiṃsa, Yāma, Tusita, Nimmānarati, or Paranimmitavasavatti devas); Upacālā recognizes Māra, rebukes him by pointing out that heavenly beings remain bound by sensual attachment, and proclaims her joy in that which neither quakes nor blazes—namely, the state beyond Māra's reach [Bodhi 2003; Collett 2014].
Scholars have noted complex variations and discrepancies in attribution between the verses of the three sisters (Cālā, Upacālā, and Sīsupacālā) in the *Therīgāthā* and the corresponding discourses in the *Bhikkhunīsaṃyutta* of the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* (SN 5.6–8) [Bodhi 2003; Bingenheimer 2008]. Parallels to Upacālā's dialogue survive in the Chinese translations of the *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the *Alternative Saṃyuktāgama* (T 100) [Bingenheimer 2008; DharmaNexus]. Additional passage-level parallels identified by SuttaCentral include Dhammapada verse 191, *Udānavarga* chapter 27, Itivuttaka 24, SN 15.10, the *Divyāvadāna*, and related verses in the *Theragāthā* (Thag 21.1) and *Therīgāthā* (Thig 7.2, 13.3, and 13.4) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports significant Pali-internal text reuse with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Cālātherīgāthā* (Thig 7.2), the *Cāpātherīgāthā* (Thig 13.3), and the *Nettippakaraṇa* (*Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*, Ne 37) [DharmaNexus].
